top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B010) rewards one identifiable discovery: firm heterogeneity and selection in trade theory. It explains exporter premia, entry and exit, and within-industry reallocation, and shows how these shape the gains from trade. These predictions go beyond representative-firm new trade theory and have been tested on firm-level data for over twenty years, so maturity is not in doubt. The Helpman-Melitz two-name credit follows the intellectual structure, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus foreign investment. The main costs are the omitted precursors (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn) and the model-dependence of welfare magnitudes. A narrow citation on the mechanism and acknowledgement in the scientific background address both. No award (P000) is ranked second because the proposal is scientifically strong and no better alternative is on the slate. This judgment rests on the merits of the contribution, not on the number of members who support it.
recusal_note: No profile-based tie to Helpman or Melitz. I am one of the explicit P001 supporters, as chair. I disclose collegial ties to Krusell and Boppart (IIES colleagues and co-authors) and to Friberg (co-author), none of whom is a candidate. The 2018 Scientific Background cites my own 2014 work, which is not on this slate. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
